Reproducible specification: construct sorted eligible IDs `E_u = catalog \ complete_training_history[u]`, excluding padding; sample independently per nonpadding target position with `E_u[torch.randperm(len(E_u), generator=g)[:32]]`. Alternatively, use equal-weight `torch.multinomial(..., 32, replacement=False, generator=g)` over eligible IDs. Require `len(E_u)>=32`; otherwise fail explicitly—replacement or fewer negatives changes the specification. User-specific exclusions preclude an unrestricted shared negative pool; independent position samples may overlap across positions. Preserve preprocessing seed 0; seed training/sampling 42, fix iteration order, save generator state, and pin software/device settings. [PyTorch sampling](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.multinomial.html), [determinism](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.use_deterministic_algorithms.html).

Flatten valid positions into `h, positive, user`, with total count `M`. For each position chunk, construct `ids=cat([positive[:,None], negatives],1)`, then `z=(h[:,None,:]*item_emb(ids)).sum(-1)/temperature`; accumulate `F.cross_entropy(z.float(), zeros, reduction='sum')/M`. This gives equal weight per position; averaging chunk means incorrectly weights short chunks. For bounded activation memory, backpropagate each scaled chunk immediately, retaining the shared encoder graph until the final chunk, then step once; concatenating losses before backward retains saved scoring tensors. Sample before scoring so chunk size does not change RNG consumption. [Cross-entropy semantics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss.html).

Analytically, eligible size changes each item's inclusion probability to `32/|E_u|`; uncorrected candidate CE is a restricted ranking objective, not unbiased full-softmax training. Dot-product norms and inverse temperature jointly control sharpness; report normalization, temperature, and regularization. Compare against explicitly defined one-negative BCE: `mean(softplus(-positive)+softplus(negative))`; averaging both labels halves this scale. Match position weighting and retune learning rate/regularization; CE couples candidates, whereas BCE uses absolute logits. [BCE implementation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/modules/loss.py).
